items.text: The minimum black hole mass used in LHC production and safety analyses is an assumed threshold of semiclassical validity, not a result about the production dynamics
items.note: The main defect is status inflation: "verified" requires evidence examined directly, yet every full-text fetch failed (403), quotes were checked only against search excerpts, and the safety-analysis leg was never directly read — by the constitution's own terms this is supported, not verified, and the reasoning's own honesty about the gap ("full-text confirmation, not evidence on the other side") is inconsistent with the flat verified label. Otherwise strong: the claim bar and canonical form are clean, the adversarial pass genuinely weighs the Plaga dissent and the threshold-estimate papers rather than waving them off, subclaims are properly at claim-bar granularity, deferred children are correctly not penalized, and 0.35 importance fits a settled methods point inside a larger debate.

items.text: Elementary particle collision outcomes depend only on center-of-mass energy, not on how the collision is produced.
items.note: The physics reasoning and adversarial pass are strong and the canonical form is clean, but "verified" contradicts the assessment's own admission that no source was actually opened (403s throughout): §10 requires evidence examined directly, so supported (confidence ~0.85) is the honest status, and the same limitation carries residual quote-accuracy/hallucination risk.

items.text: In semiclassical TeV-scale gravity models, a black hole produced at the LHC has initial mass of order the parton center-of-mass energy, with production described only above a minimum mass several times the fundamental Planck scale
items.note: The reasoning explicitly states both founding-paper quotations could not be verified against full text (arXiv fetches returned 403), which is incompatible with "verified": the evidence was examined indirectly, so supported is the correct status. Otherwise the claim is well-formed, corroboration from independent later practice is genuine, and the decomposition sensibly stops where the discourse stops.

items.text: Quantum black hole models used to design LHC searches identify the black hole production threshold mass with the fundamental Planck scale itself
items.note: Status "verified" is miscalibrated: the reasoning itself admits the primary papers could not be fetched (403s) and the readings rest on search-surfaced excerpts, which under §10 is indirect evidence and therefore at most "supported." The hallucination risk follows — verbatim quotes accepted from search snippets, and one URL (0912.0826) is cited for both the ATLAS and CMS points. Substantively the assessment is careful: the adversarial pass correctly distinguishes the semiclassical several-times-the-scale convention, and unassessed children are properly not counted against it.

items.text: Collisions at the Large Hadron Collider present no danger to the Earth or the public.
items.note: The assessment is genuinely strong — convergent independent lines, a real adversarial pass, honest recording of the 403 gap — but "verified" is miscalibrated on the standard's own terms: the primary PDFs and SPC report were never directly examined (only abstracts/excerpts via search), so §10's verified bar ("evidence, examined directly") is not met; supported at ~0.9 would be the honest status. Note also that the reasoning refers to the subclaim set only implicitly; the child "Nature has already produced LHC-equivalent collisions" is marked verified despite the assessment's own acknowledgment of a fixed-target kinematics quibble, and that verification was granted without recorded direct examination either. The absolute "no danger" canonical form is roughly what the debate is about and is acceptable.

items.text: Hawking's semiclassical evaporation calculation applies to black holes as small as those the LHC could produce.
items.note: A well-argued supported verdict: the reasoning explicitly weighs the dissent (Plaga's model-internal condition, the 10^23 rederivation, terascale modeling-insufficiency claims) and explains why neither contested nor verified fits, with an honest note that sources were read via excerpts (403s). Defects: subclaims are cited by opaque IDs, and the claim text omits the mass-regime conditionality the reasoning treats as load-bearing — a reader of the bare claim cannot see that applicability is defended only several Planck scales above threshold, which is why the canonical form reads understated/frame-loose rather than neutral-precise.

items.text: In the Casadio-Harms model the threshold mass below which mass loss is suppressed is of order the fundamental Planck scale
items.note: The reasoning is unusually honest — it flags its own order-of-magnitude inference as the cap on status and names what would move the verdict — but the child layer has an outright defect: the same anti-premise appears twice (once "none", once "contradicts") with empty labels, an opaque-ids problem, and sources were read only via excerpts after 403s, which "supported" at 0.78 absorbs but does not fully disclose in the claim text.

items.text: Microscopic black holes, if produced at the LHC, would evaporate almost immediately through Hawking radiation.
items.note: A model assessment: it weighs the Plaga dissent and rebuttal exchange on the merits, explains why supported-not-verified, and states what would change the verdict. Minor flaw: it records credence 0.93 in prose while the claim stores no credence, and "almost immediately" sits slightly stronger than the seconds-long-survival scenarios it itself cites.

items.text: Every black hole production mechanism proposed for the LHC produces holes with masses a few times the fundamental Planck scale or higher, not at or below the fundamental scale.
items.note: A well-argued contested verdict that weighs both sides honestly and discloses source-access limits, though the instance count is slightly inflated (Plaga's "denial" is dismissed in the reasoning's own reading, yet still tallied as a denying source), and the universal "Every" claim is at the upper edge of what the evidence supports without a credence figure.

items.text: In some quantum black hole models, Hawking radiation is suppressed below a Planck-scale threshold mass, so microscopic black holes could persist.
items.note: A well-scoped, honestly hedged assessment: the 403/excerpt limitation is disclosed and matched to the supported status, and the semiclassical-endpoint counter-position is weighed rather than dismissed. The main residue is that subclaims are addressed by UUID alongside their glosses, which taxes readability, and confidence 0.72 sits slightly high for a verdict resting entirely on unverified excerpts of three mutually non-independent theoretical papers.

items.text: Cosmic-ray collisions on astronomical bodies reach LHC-scale energies and vastly outnumber the entire LHC programme.
items.note: A strong, genuinely verified assessment: independent flux integration and fixed-target kinematics establish the physics directly, the lopsided source set is candidly acknowledged rather than treated as independent corroboration, and the search for counterevidence (which found safety-inference disputes, not energy/count disputes) is honestly reported. Verified at 0.9 is the right call even though two key sources were excerpt-level, since the verdict does not hinge on them. Minor defects only: subclaims are referenced by opaque ids (a7b78f06, 6b39f037) in the reasoning body, and the count conjunct's own node remains unassessed — a legitimate deferral under §19, but the graph should fund it soon since the compound's "verified" rests partly on the steward's own arithmetic being correct.

items.text: Nature has already produced LHC-equivalent collisions throughout the universe many times over without harmful consequences.
items.note: The verified status is earned for the occurrence half — the fixed-target kinematics and flux arithmetic are independently derived, not deferred to CERN — but the claim text outruns what the verdict defends: "without harmful consequences" (unqualified, universe-wide) is silently re-read in prose as "no harm observed or attributed," and that "observed" qualifier belongs in the canonical form itself, since Ord et al.'s anthropic-luck scenario is credible argument against the unqualified reading. Graph hygiene defect: the air-shower subclaim appears twice verbatim with conflicting edge types ([supports] and [requires]).
